title: Recent Change in Lesion Appearance
explanation: Patient reports recent changes in the lesion's appearance (color, shape, or border). Evolving lesions ('E' in ABCDE criteria) are a primary clinical indication for dermatological evaluation.
suggestedNextStep: Schedule a prompt in-person dermatological examination and bring any prior photos for comparison.

title: Spontaneous or Recurrent Bleeding
explanation: Lesion bleeding or crusting without major trauma can reflect epidermal fragility or ulceration seen in basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or nodular melanoma.
suggestedNextStep: Seek timely clinical evaluation by a dermatologist; avoid picking or applying home remedies.

title: Progressive Lesion Growth
explanation: Reported increase in lesion size warrants clinical assessment, particularly when combined with pigmentation changes or surface elevation.
suggestedNextStep: Arrange an in-person skin exam to measure and monitor lesion dimensions with dermoscopy.

title: Diameter >= 6 mm
explanation: A lesion diameter of 6 mm or greater aligns with the 'D' threshold in ABCDE melanoma screening guidelines, though smaller lesions can also be malignant.
suggestedNextStep: Include lesion measurement during your dermatological consultation.

title: Personal History of Skin Cancer
explanation: Prior skin cancer significantly increases baseline risk for subsequent cutaneous malignancies (both melanoma and keratinocyte carcinomas).
suggestedNextStep: Maintain scheduled full-body skin surveillance with a dermatologist.

title: Family History of Skin Cancer
explanation: A family history of skin cancer (especially melanoma in first-degree relatives) is an established inherited and shared-exposure risk factor.
suggestedNextStep: Mention family history during clinical screening and practice consistent photoprotection.

title: Lesion Pain or Tenderness
explanation: Tenderness or pain on palpation can occur with inflamed lesions, squamous cell carcinoma, or rapidly expanding nodules.
suggestedNextStep: Have a clinician inspect the tender lesion in person.

title: Persistent or Moderate-to-Severe Itching
explanation: Localized pruritus can be associated with actinic keratoses, inflammatory lesions, or symptomatic superficial malignancies.
suggestedNextStep: Avoid scratching and mention itching duration to your physician.

title: Elevated / Raised Surface
explanation: Elevation is seen across both benign lesions (seborrheic keratosis, dermal nevus) and nodular malignancies (BCC, SCC, nodular melanoma).
suggestedNextStep: Evaluate elevation alongside border, color, and change history.

title: UV-Sensitive Fitzpatrick Phototype (I–II)
explanation: Fitzpatrick skin types I and II burn easily and tan minimally, carrying elevated lifetime UV sensitivity.
suggestedNextStep: Prioritize daily broad-spectrum SPF 30+ sunscreen and protective clothing.

title: Chronically Sun-Exposed Anatomical Site
explanation: Chronically sun-exposed sites experience higher cumulative UV radiation and higher incidence of ACK, BCC, and SCC.
suggestedNextStep: Include high-exposure anatomical sites in routine skin examinations.

title: Age >= 60 Years
explanation: Cumulative sun damage over decades increases the baseline prevalence of actinic keratosis, keratinocyte carcinomas, and seborrheic keratosis.
suggestedNextStep: Schedule periodic preventive skin checks with a healthcare provider.
